column3: NASB renders “inexcusable” as “without excuse” and “judging” as “passes judgment.”
NASB renders “is according to truth upon” as “rightly falls upon.”
NASB adds “when” and “the same.”
NASB renders “despise” as “think lightly of.”
NASB renders “hardness” as “stubbornness,” “treasuring up” as “storing up,” and the single word for “righteous judgment” as such.
The quotation is in capitals; “works” is rendered “DEEDS.” A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB renders “endurance in good work” as “perseverance in doing good.”
NASB renders “of self-interest” as “selfishly ambitious,” “being persuaded by” as “obey,” and “anger” as “indignation.”
NASB adds “There will be.”
NASB adds “also.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “in the Law” as “under the Law.”
NASB follows the critical text; “righteous” is rendered “just.”
NASB follows the critical text; “by nature” is rendered “instinctively.”
NASB adds “in that” and renders “between one another” as “alternately.”
NASB renders the verb as “will judge” and moves “according to my gospel” forward.
NASB follows the critical text (“But if”); “you are called a Jew” is rendered “you bear the name ‘Jew.’”
NASB adds “His” and renders “the things being superior” as “the things that are essential.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “instructor” as “corrector” and “infants” as “the immature,” and it reorders the verse.
NASB adds “one should.”
NASB adds “one should.”
NASB renders “transgression” as “breaking” and adds “your.”
The quotation is in capitals.
NASB renders “profits” as “is of value” and “do” as “practice.”
NASB renders “the uncircumcision” as “the uncircumcised man” and “reckoned” as “regarded.”
NASB turns the verse into a question, adding “will not … will he not,” and renders “by nature” as “physically”; it adds “if he keeps” and “though having.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “in spirit” as “by the Spirit.”
